thread:
maria.s: Quick sync — we need a concrete checklist for audit event visibility differences between tenant admins vs members. Customer asked for clarity on what their admins can see after the schema + RBAC changes.
aj: Agreed. Short Qs: 1) do admins get cross-tenant visibility? 2) can members request exports? 3) are signed events surfaceable to customers?
kevin: 1) No cross-tenant by default. Any cross-tenant view requires org-level role + approved contract. 2) Members shouldn't be able to trigger exports that contain other users' PII. 3) We sign events with KMS — we can present signature metadata to customers.
chloe: PII redaction: do we strip fields before storing or mark them and redact at query time? Both have tradeoffs.
maria.s: For compliance, store only minimal PII and keep raw in a separate encrypted blob that requires KMS unwrap + privileged role to access. Query-time redaction easier for UX but harder for guarantees.
aj: Proposal: add fields to audit schema: `principal_role`, `viewer_scope`, `redaction_mask`, `kms_signature_id`, `export_requestor_id`. Backwards compatible versioned schema v2.
kevin: +1 on versioning. Also add `tenant_view_mask` which enumerates which tenant-scoped fields are visible to the token used to fetch.
chloe: Example event we can show customers (safe):

```
{
  "ts": 1768423456000,
  "tenant_id": "t-987",
  "actor": "user:alice",
  "principal_role": "member",
  "action": "create_api_key",
  "resource": "api_key:***",
  "viewer_scope": "tenant_member",
  "kms_signature_id": "sig-2026-05",
  "redaction_mask": ["secret_value"]
}
```

chloe: We should avoid exposing `resource` raw value for members (masking) but admins with `audit:read_full` can see full resource with KMS audit unwrap.
samir: How do scoped tokens factor in? We have scoped tokens used by internal analytics and by customer audit consumers.
kevin: Scoped tokens should carry `audit_scope` claim: `member`, `admin`, `exporter`. Our query layer uses that to compute `viewer_scope` and apply `tenant_view_mask`.
diane: For customer-facing signed events: customers want to validate event integrity. We can provide the event plus `kms_signature_id` and a verification endpoint that returns the public key metadata.
aj: Ops question: indexing. New fields must be indexed by `tenant_id`, `action`, `ts`. `kms_signature_id` only indexed for lookup when verifying exports.
maria.s: Tests to add to validation suite:
- Member token returns events with masked fields and no `kms_signature_id` disclosure for masked fields.
- Admin token (with `audit:read_full`) returns full events and can initiate export.
- Scoped token with `exporter` can request export but export payload must be pre-approved and signed.
- Attempted cross-tenant access rejected with 403 and logged.
kevin: Also add regression: existing integrators that parse previous schema shouldn't break. Add a compatibility flag `schema_version` default `v1` if absent.
chloe: UI-level: in Console, show a hover tooltip explaining why some fields are masked and a link to request unmask (audit request workflow).
samir: For export approval, require 2 approvers for any export containing PII. Workflow ties into KMS unwrap permissions.
diane: Incident scenario: if a customer claims tampering, they call support -> we pull signed events, run verification, produce signed report. That requires us to keep verification logs for N days per compliance.
aj: Who owns implementing KMS signature metadata + verification endpoint? I can take schema + API contract. Kevin, can infra carve out the verification endpoint and key rotation story?
kevin: I can allocate sprint work. Need spec: endpoint `/audit/verify?tenant_id=...&event_ts=...` returns `verified:true|false`, `kms_signature_id`, `public_key_id`, `signed_by`.
maria.s: Also add audit export retention policy to policy docs and note that exported signed bundles are customer-responsibility once delivered.
chloe: Edge-case: service accounts (system) actions — visibility rules: platform admins can see system account actions across tenants for SRE, but must be audited and require override perms.
aj: We'll draft a one-page checklist and an open PR for schema changes. Timeline: draft by EOD Friday, PR by next Tue, tests by next Thu.
samir: I'm going to write test cases for scoped tokens.
diane: I'll update incident runbook to include signed-event verification steps.
audit-bot: Deploy scheduled: schema-v2-migration job queued for 2026-06-01 02:00 UTC. :hammer_and_wrench:
maria.s: Thanks everyone. If anyone has objections to the `viewer_scope` naming or something, post here before EOD. Otherwise I'll create the PR with the fields listed above.
